title: Audit Log Monitoring

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.3.1 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.3.1 search returns zero rows.

knownFalsePositives: Our own break-glass and automation accounts show up the same as anyone else, and a delete or write during a change window is expected. We allowlist the roles that do routine maintenance and we link alerts to approved changes before we call an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `google:gcp:pubsub:message`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `messageId` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Create a Pub/Sub topic and subscription. Configure a log sink to route audit logs to Pub/Sub. Set up Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform with a Pub/Sub input. Alert on destructive operations (delete, setIamPolicy).
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" logName="*activity"
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.1_audit_log_monitoring_1"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:pubsub:message` in `index=gcp` to detect audit log monitoring. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `messageId` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_1_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (principal, method, count), Bar chart, Timeline..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of audit log monitoring so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
